links.comparator_used: Baseline single-pass generation without validation-repair (paired baseline condition)
links.outcome: Schema compliance of structured outputs (ICD-10, CPT, HL7 FHIR) across 960 model-scenario pairs
links.effect: Compliance rose from baseline 85.9-91.6% to 99.0% overall (98.4-99.4% across models); absolute improvements of 7.8 to 12.5 percentage points; exact McNemar p<0.001
links.tradeoff: Repair requires iterative loops; most errors resolved within one or two iterations (extra generation passes).
links.quote: Third, the validation-repair framework achieves 99.0 percent overall compliance, ranging from 98.4 to 99.4 percent across models, with most errors resolving within one or two iterations.

links.comparator_used: Baseline condition without validation (unvalidated model outputs)
links.outcome: Schema compliance of structured outputs against ICD-10, CPT, and FHIR standards
links.effect: Compliance improved from 85.9-91.6% at baseline to 99.0% overall with validation-repair; improvements of 7.8 to 12.5 percentage points; McNemar p<0.001
links.tradeoff: Repair loop needed one or two iterations for most errors.
links.quote: Exact McNemar p-values below 0.001 and absolute improvements of 7.8 to 12.5 percentage points across model sizes confirm statistical significance.
